subject: Re: [GGIR] Is Imputation Possible Only in Middle (Not Ends) of Collection Period?

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Is Imputation Possible Only in Middle (Not Ends) of Collection Period?
parts:
Hi Joanna,

GGIR facilitates masking segments of the recordings based on your study protocol as you already discovered: https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/chapter5_StudyProtocol.html

The masked periods are always imputed. This is needed in case any part of them ends up being used as part of a valid recording day. For example, if you only mask the first 2 hours of the first day then that day may still be valid, but we need those first 2 hours imputed. However, when large parts or even entire days are considered invalid then those are excluded from all csv reports, so for those days it does not matter whether we impute or not.

The only place where you will still see those imputed days of data is in the visual reports, which intentionally show the entire original time series to avoid any misunderstanding about the duration of a recording.

If it is important to you that visual report show non-imputed data for invalid days then I am happy to develop that as part of a paid consultancy. Please pm me if you are interested.

Best,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/


On Tuesday, 18 February 2025 at 10:29 PM, joeck...@gmail.com <joeck...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi GGIR Users,

I have noticed in several of my participants (total sample = 68 participants) that in the end (sometimes also in the beginning) of their GeneActiv collection period, there are several days of non-wear imputed data. This is clearly from when the participants collection period ended and they took the watch off, but the watch kept recording nonwear for several days. I would want this data completely deleted and not used.

In an ideal world, there would be a setting for GGIR where the beginning and end of collection period were excluded if nonwear is detected, and then only data within the beginning and end of wear time is imputed where necessary and used in analyses. Is there such a setting for this specific scenario? I have looked through all GGIR parameters, but do not believe there is. Please let me know if there is an alternative way to accomplish this.

I would use data_masking_strategy = 1 and specify hrs.del.start and hrs.del.end, but each of the participants wore the accelerometer for a different number of days, so this wouldn't be possible unless I did them 1 at a time.

I think my current best option is to do data_masking_strategy = 5 and then specify ndayswindow = 30, as on average participants completed 30 days. I will go with this if needed, but I wanted to ask first if there is any other option for cutting out nonwear at the beginning and end of collection period that could be applied to a large number of participants.

Thank you for your help!
Best,
Joanna

Hi Dr. van Hees, 

Thank you for your response. I realized after I made my original post that, just as you have said, with includeadaycrit =16 that those days of all nonwear would be excluded from processing anyways. So my concerns with nonwear contributing to outputs is addressed with that. 

It is good to know though that masked periods are always imputed in case the day still has enough hours to meet includeadaycrit. That makes more sense, thank you very much!!

All my best,
Joanna
